issues.evidence: SYSTEM-REGISTRY.md requires the latest reconciliation run to name every public report and to contain a decision for every active registry asset with reconciliation_required:true. The current registry marks seven assets as requiring reconciliation: global-dependency-network, structural-opportunity-atlas, strategic-actors, resource-control-atlas, policy-case-atlas, conflict-systems and technology-signal-ledger. The current data/reconciliation-ledger.json ends at 2026-11-16T11:08:58.922Z; its latest run, 2026-11-16-global-macro-publication-reconciliation, names only MT-GM-2026-11-16. No run names MT-GM-2026-11-19. This report materially covers Hormuz oil/LNG flows and bypass routes, the Middle East war and maritime-security exposure, grid and pipeline investment requirements, and electricity-equipment constraints. At minimum, the dependency network, structural opportunity atlas and conflict systems require explicit evidence-based decisions; the registry still requires a recorded decision for all seven assets, including not_applicable or deferred_evidence_gap where justified. Without that append-only reconciliation record, the report cannot enter the public corpus without violating the registry rule.

source_integrity.summary: The current main tree and Git blob SHAs were re-read for the v2 pending sidecar and both staged Markdown editions. No current-revision approval, rejection or public metadata exists.

source_vintage_and_cutoff.summary: The declared cutoff is 2026-11-19 09:01 UTC. The Reuters oil observation at 04:55 GMT and Asian snapshot at 03:51 GMT precede it. The IEA WEO page is dated 19 November; an embargo advisory states the embargo lifted at 08:00 Antalya (05:00 UTC), before cutoff, although the IEA report page itself does not show an exact publication hour.

factual_methodology.summary: The main quantitative claims were checked against the IEA WEO 2026 and November Oil Market Report, EIA weekly petroleum data, Federal Reserve minutes, US Treasury yields, World Bank International Debt Report, Eurostat HICP, Reuters market reporting and Brazilian/Asian market sources. The report distinguishes scenario requirements from committed projects and observed flows from modelled pathways.

evidence_traceability.summary: Fourteen references are used consistently across EN/PT-BR. Primary-source anchors include IEA, EIA, Federal Reserve, US Treasury, World Bank and Eurostat; Reuters, AP, UOL and The Edge provide dated market/event context. The report explicitly records the absence of harmonised private credit-spread and project-level capex/disbursement data.

Nine analytical sections, contrary evidence and conditional scenarios are present. The separate strict editorial-depth job failed only on seven other staged items; this candidate was not among them. The main production build and visual-output validation passed.

contrary_evidence: Brent and WTI fell on 18 November and US commercial crude inventories rose in the week ended 13 November, consistent with a looser near-term crude balance.
The IEA expects oil supply to rebound in 2027, which could lower benchmark prices if the forecast materialises.
India's rupee remained resilient despite a stronger dollar, with reported November equity inflows supporting the currency.
US crude and distillate inventories increased in the latest weekly EIA balance, even while the IEA describes low global on-land stocks and tight diesel markets.
The IEA's grid and pipeline figures are system requirements and scenario assumptions, not proof of project bankability or implementation.
limitations: The exact publication hour of the IEA World Energy Outlook 2026 is not stated on its 19 November page.
IEA scenarios and system requirements are modelled pathways, not realised infrastructure, committed capital or guaranteed policy outcomes.
The 7 mb/d pipeline figure includes projects under construction or consideration; the Low Hormuz Case depends on multiple conditional assumptions.
US EIA inventories are a national weekly observation and cannot establish global diesel availability.
Treasury par yields do not measure private credit spreads, project-finance margins or sovereign borrowing spreads.
The Asian equity figures are delayed intraday observations at 03:51 GMT, not closing returns.
The World Bank debt aggregates are not energy-project debt and do not identify the financing terms of individual infrastructure projects.
The Brazil market move reflects domestic fiscal uncertainty as well as external dollar and rate conditions.
notes: One new rejection for revision 1. This is a publication-readiness failure in the mandatory system-registry reconciliation gate, not a finding that the report's core energy-market analysis is factually unsound. No approval or publication authorization was created. The producer must append the reconciliation run and update the pending sidecar last; QA must then review the new exact SHA set. No public report, index, CSS, taxonomy or institutional content was changed.
